source.title: Low-Pass Filtering SGD for Recovering Flat Optima in the Deep Learning Optimization Landscape
source.authors: Devansh Bisla; Jing Wang; A. Choromańska

record.file_problem: none; full paper and supplementary material are present
record.tranche_reason: Measures correlations between several loss sharpness measures and generalization gaps across model and optimizer settings. This is a conceptual test of whether measured network properties track the gap, using a different sharpness measure and experimental setup.
record.gate_note: The paper measures the relationship between generalization gap and sharpness measures; it does not test arbitrary-label memorization, widening past interpolation, or the other claim versions. Table 2 reports correlations aggregated over model sets, not individual model results. Cited results from other studies are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study measures generalization correlations with alternative sharpness scores, but does not evaluate V7's magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance before training error rises. Its other experiments do not establish the comparisons specified by V1–V6 or V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the correlation findings, but omits the paper's central optimizer conclusion: the authors derive LPF-SGD and report favorable held-out performance against several baselines. They also report that LPF tracks double descent. Their theoretical result compares generalization-error upper bounds for original and smoothed losses; smaller upper bounds alone do not establish smaller actual generalization error.
record.recipe_differences: Compares correlations of LPF and several other sharpness measures with generalization gap across ResNet18 hyperparameter sweeps, rather than using the specific magnitude-scaled perturbation measure and model family in V7.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured correlation changes with the varied hyperparameter: LPF correlation is negative for width and weak for batch normalization, but positive for momentum, weight decay, learning rate, batch size, and skip connections.

fits_no_version.finding: LPF sharpness correlates positively with generalization gap overall and in several hyperparameter sweeps, negatively across widths, and weakly across batch-normalization settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Expected loss under fixed Gaussian weight perturbations of balanced networks tracks generalization gaps in some CIFAR-10 ResNet18 comparisons, with substantial dependence on the varied hyperparameter.

fits_no_version.finding: The local-entropy gradient norm has an overall gap correlation of −0.064±0.04.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Alternative landscape scores differ substantially in their ability to rank generalization gaps.

fits_no_version.finding: LPF sharpness has gap correlations of 0.867 with label noise and 0.916 with input noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fixed-noise LPF sharpness tracks generalization gaps across label- and input-corruption levels in CIFAR-10 ResNet18 models.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 11.4 reports width-dependent double descent and an LPF–validation-error correlation of 0.851 for ResNet18 trained for 4000 epochs with Adam and 20% label noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LPF sharpness can track width-dependent validation-error double descent; establishing improvement beyond interpolation additionally requires training-error measurements.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics
record.problems: The correlation experiment uses one architecture family and one dataset; results are aggregated over model sets varying one hyperparameter at a time. The text notes that the study does not span multiple datasets and models because the experiment required approximately 9000 GPU hours. Noise-setting correlations are provided in figure titles rather than tables.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying results for V7 were left out. Table 2 comparisons for other sharpness measures are not separately recorded except for μLE, the lowest overall correlation, because the extracted rows focus on LPF tracking and the comparison needed to support its stated ranking. Other sections report optimizer performance and adversarial robustness, which do not measure the claim versions' named behaviors.

untested.parts: Paired random-label fitting and natural-label generalization using the same architectures and recipes, including chance held-out accuracy with random labels.
Continued test-error improvement beyond an established zero-training-error width threshold. Figure 7 reports double descent without reporting training errors or locating that threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under the specified tuning regimes; translation experiments compare Adam-based methods with one another.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under a fixed epoch budget and adaptations that remove the penalty.
Controlled addition or removal of dropout.

Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance before training error rises, its association with generalization gaps, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures. Balancing weights before measuring fixed-noise expected loss does not supply this measure.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All extracted correlation values match the supplied text. The row states are cannot_determine relative to the supplied claim versions, not judgments that the reported correlations are unreadable. Network balancing addresses parameter scaling but does not turn LPF expected loss into V7's training-error tolerance measure. No original-source exclusion applies.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label test performance.
Test error as width increases beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD held-out performance under different tuning regimes.
Large-batch versus small-batch held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets.
Effects of dropout and its removal on held-out error.

The paper tests sharpness-gap correlations, but not the specific magnitude-scaled perturbation measure described in this version, the CIFAR-10 and SVHN setup, or comparison with margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.
